title: Zima (1992–2008): the clear malt drink Coors pulled
description: Zima was Coors’s clear, citrus-flavored malt drink. It sold about 1.3 million barrels in 1994, volume fell about 49% in 1995, and U.S. production ended in 2008.

card.blurb: Coors filtered the color and the taste out of a beer, added citrus and spent tens of millions telling America it was zomething different. Most drinkers tried it once.

hero.dates: Test-marketed from September 1992. U.S. production ended October 10, 2008.
hero.standfirst: It was not a beer and not a wine cooler. For one year, that was enough.
hero.deck: Zima was a clear, citrus-flavored malt drink that Coors launched in 1992 and that was withdrawn in the United States in 2008. It was [a product, not a company](/category/consumer/), so there was no bankruptcy. Coors sold about 1.3 million barrels of it in one year and roughly half as many the next. The brand then survived for thirteen more years on reformulations and has come back twice since as a summer novelty. The sources are Coors’s SEC filings, the press of the time and the brand’s own archived website. Where a figure is not public, [the page says so](#sources).

findings.title: Trial was never the problem.
findings.text: Coors estimated that 70% of America’s regular drinkers tried Zima in 1994.[^13] The brand manager called the trial curve “so huge we almost hit 1.3 million barrels.”[^12]

findings.title: Repeat purchase was.
findings.text: Coors’s 10-K for 1995 says Zima volumes fell about 49% from the launch year. In the second quarter of 1995 the fall was about 60%.[^3][^12]

findings.title: The drop hurt because Zima was profitable.
findings.text: The same filing says Zima had a higher gross profit percentage than Coors’s other brands, so lower Zima volume cut the company’s gross margin from 36.1% to 34.8%.[^3]

findings.title: Men were the target, and men left.
findings.text: The agency that made the ads conceded in 1995 that the drink was “invited to be seen as wussy.”[^12] Zima Gold, built to win men back, was withdrawn within the year.[^3]

findings.title: The name outlived the product.
findings.text: After the 2008 withdrawal Zima stayed on sale in Japan, returned to U.S. shelves for the summers of 2017 and 2018, and was relaunched in Japan in 2023.[^26][^30][^31]
